'''Elica Le Bon''' is an Iranian-heritage attorney, human-rights activist, and political commentator. Born and raised in London to Iranian parents and later based in Los Angeles, she trained and worked as a lawyer before turning to full-time advocacy. She is covered in [[Media and Personalities]] as part of the commentary-and-debate arena: a voice built around Iran, human rights, and "propaganda debunking," written here for what she actually argues rather than as a verdict.

== Who she is ==

Le Bon's family carries the memory of the 1979 revolution directly — her mother and aunt were imprisoned in its aftermath — and that lineage frames much of her work. Her public profile rose sharply during the '''Woman, Life, Freedom''' movement that followed the 2022 death in custody of '''Mahsa Amini''', when she became one of the more visible diaspora voices explaining the protests to Western audiences. She has since built a following in the high hundreds of thousands across platforms and appeared on outlets from Piers Morgan and Dr. Phil to MSNBC, Fox News, and NewsNation — a reach that cuts across the usual left/right media split.

== What she argues ==

Her core throughline is advocacy for the Iranian people against the Islamic Republic: amplifying protesters, pushing back on what she characterizes as regime talking points in Western discourse, and arguing for secular, rights-based politics. A recurring format is '''"propaganda debunking"''' — taking a widely-shared claim about Iran or the wider Middle East and arguing it is regime-serving or factually wrong. She has also taken strong, and more contested, positions in the Iran–Israel arena, including defending Israel and criticizing those she sees as aligned with the Islamic Republic.

== The strong case ==

She is an articulate, first-hand diaspora advocate for a cause — Iranian women's and human rights — that is too often flattened or ignored in Western coverage, and she is effective at reaching audiences who would otherwise never engage it. Her insistence on distinguishing the Iranian people from the regime that rules them is an important and frequently-missed distinction, and her willingness to appear across hostile and friendly media alike gives the argument unusually broad exposure.

== The weak / contested case ==

She is a polarizing figure, and fairly so: her geopolitical positions — especially on Israel and on questions of war and intervention — are sharply contested, and critics argue that "propaganda debunking" can itself become a frame that hardens one side's narrative. As with any single advocate, her analysis is a strong point of view, not a neutral brief; this Library points to her as a voice worth engaging, and recommends reading her alongside other perspectives on the same events (see [[SoapBox Politics]] and [[SoapBox Oversight]]) rather than as the last word.
